info.title: Converting an &ay; profile to an &agama; profile

abstract.para: Convert an &ay; profile with the &agama; CLI and verify the resulting &agama; profile, including its requirements and important differences to check after conversion.

section.title: What &agama; does with an &ay; profile
section.para: The agama config generate command accepts a path or URL and converts its content into a native &agama; JSON configuration. It recognizes an &ay; profile automatically: if the given path or URL ends in .xml, .erb, or a trailing slash (for a rules or classes directory), &agama; downloads and processes it as &ay; content, evaluating any Embedded Ruby (ERB) templating or rules/classes selection along the way, before converting the result to JSON. Any other input is treated as an already &agama;-native JSON or Jsonnet profile and passed through unchanged.

note.title: Automatic conversion at boot time
note.para: You do not need to run agama config generate yourself to start an unattended installation. If you point the inst.auto boot parameter, or one of &agama;'s predefined profile locations, directly at an &ay; profile, &agama; performs the same conversion automatically before installing. Manually converting the profile first, as described in this topic, is only necessary if you want to review the result beforehand—recommended, since the converter silently omits unsupported &ay; elements instead of reporting them.

section.para: &agama; is not a drop-in replacement for &ay;, and the conversion does not cover every &ay; section. For the exact list of which &ay; elements are supported, and which &agama; field they map to, refer to .

section.title: Troubleshooting missing settings and conversion errors

listitem.para: If the installed system is missing configuration that was present in the original &ay; profile, check for that section. &agama; reports an unsupported field in the Web interface when the profile is loaded, though a command started from the CLI shows no further output until the field is acknowledged in the Web interface.

If your &ay; profile relies heavily on the partitioning section and converting it to the native &agama; storage format is impractical, consider using the legacyAutoyastStorage section instead, described in Advanced storage configuration using &agama; profiles.
